mechanism_claims.claim_text: Metamarin increases Mtb ClpC1 ATPase activity in an in vitro ATPase assay; this supports ClpC1 pathway engagement but is not a direct binding-site measurement.
mechanism_claims.direct_assay_type: BIOMOL Green ClpC1 ATPase activity assay
mechanism_claims.assay_conditions: ClpC1 1 uM and ATP 100 uM in Tris/KCl/MgCl2 buffer, pH 7.5; metamarin tested at 0.1, 1.0, and 10 uM; 37 C for 1 h plus BIOMOL Green readout; three independent experiments.

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=Antimicrobial Activity and Mode of Action of 1

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper reports functional ATPase stimulation and compares behavior to cyclomarin A; it does not provide direct binding constants or structural binding evidence for metamarin.
direct_assay_types: BIOMOL Green ClpC1 ATPase activity assay

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Metamarin increases proteolytic activity of the Mtb ClpC1/P1/P2 complex in a FITC-casein degradation assay, consistent with uncontrolled protein degradation as the proposed killing mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: compound 1/metamarin against Mtb ClpC1/P1/P2 protease complex
mechanism_claims.assay_conditions: ClpC1 1 uM, ClpP1/P2 2 uM, FITC-casein 0.3 uM, ATP 2 mM; metamarin tested at 0.1, 1.0, and 10 uM; fluorescence monitored at 485/535 nm; three independent experiments.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Metamarin inhibits intracellular Mtb growth in infected J774A.1 macrophages with IC50 0.71 ug/mL; this is phenotypic support for antimycobacterial activity, not a standalone direct mechanism claim.
mechanism_claims.assay_conditions: J774A.1 macrophage infection with Mtb mc2 6206 harboring mLux plasmid; 72 h treatment; luminescence viability endpoint; triplicate treatments and two complete experiments.
